newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Nov trade surplus rises to C$1.82 bln.
newsitem.headline: Canada Nov trade surplus rises to C$1.82 bln.

text.p: Canada's merchandise trade surplus widended in November to C$1.82 billion from C$1.53 billion in October (revised from C$1.49 billion), Statistics Canada said on Friday. Canada's imports rose 4.7 percent in November to a record C$20.57 billion, it said.
Note: Figures in billions of current Canadian dollars, on a balance of payments basis, seasonally adjusted.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a surplus of C$2.92 billion in November. The survey also forecast imports of C$20.19 billion and exports of C$23.09 billion in November.

Statistics Canada said exports rose 5.7 percent in November, boosted by automotive shipments which regained two thirds of the losses caused by the October strike at General Motors Corp's Canadian unit.

The rise in imports was led by a surge in aircraft purchases and a rebound in auto parts imports. Gains in imports from the United States and the European Union were tempered by declines in imports from all other trading partners, Statistics Canada said.
The agency said a stronger trade balance with the United States, Canada's main trading partner, accounted for most of the overall increase in the country's trade surplus in November.
